description: Hello! We come from distinct parts of the world creating a simple mars outpost game to encourage kids age 7-15 to challenge their critical thinking and decision-making skills to survive on mars by choosing which facilities to prioritize, build, and protect
summary:
Our team Mars Based Research Department developed a grid-base survival game “Outpost Architect”, to address the “Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge by allowing kids age 7-15 place essential modules such as Solar Panels, Habitat Pods, Radiation Shield, and Medical Bays to decide which modules to build and protect to maintain crew’s health and food supply during events such as a dust storm. 

This project aims to streamlines understanding of aerospace engineering concepts to young learners. Space missions requires detailed planning, resource allocation and management, and make critical decisions under pressure. However, these concepts are often hard to understand through traditional STEM learning materials. By turning these challenges into an interactive and engaging strategy game, “Outpost Architect” provides a fun learning experience to encourage students to challenge their problem-solving skills and experience joining a space mission engineer and commander.
details:
Project Overview

Our team’s ‘Outpost Architect’ is a 2D grid-based resource management game allowing young learners to experience the challenges of managing and maintaining resources in a simulated Mars outpost. Players pretend to become a mission commander to design a sustainable base with limited budget and grid-space. 

The gameplay involves players strategically placing, prioritizing, and protect modules from solar radiation such as: solar panel, Habitation pods, Hydroponics, Radiation Shields, Medical Bay. Each module has different construction costs, power and manpower requirements, and functions. Players must critically think under pressure to decide which module to build to carefully balance electricity use, radiation protection, and crew’s health to maintain the outpost’s operations.

The game also has a hazardous event, that is a dust storm, threatening the crew’s health. Players have to manage operational costs and prioritize resources to overcome these challenges. To win the game, players fill a certain percentage of the grids, which increases as the players level up: 20%, 40%, and 60% of their grid in three respective levels.

Benefits and Education Value

The game allows interactive learning experience for future space engineers by evaluating the immediate consequences of their decisions, and gain educational benefits such as but not limited to:

Resource management: Choose between different opportunity costs of balancing resources, power consumption, and energy generation

Critical thinking and problem-solving: encourages players to understand and choose risks, predict risks, think of solutions to make decisions strategically under pressure

Scientific awareness: exposing students to environmental challenge and technological requirements to maintain settlement outside the Earth

Intended impact

Our project’s goals is to inspire the young generation to learn STEM subjects with our approachable, accessible, and enjoyable mars outpost simulation and to solve space-mission challenges. Through our project’s gameplay, students develop problem-solving skills, critical-thinking skills, and decision-making skills crucial for the youth’s intellectual development. Additionally, our project’s lightweight design, is suitable for classroom activities and independent learning without special hardware. 

Tools and Technologies

Our team collaborated and developed  “Outpost Architect” on GitHub for source-code management, using programming languages: typescript, CSS, HTML. Our team custom-designed 2D module icons using Canva and used  ChatGPT to increase the graphics and resolution of the module’s design, and generate solely the game’s background. 

Creativity and Design Considerations

Our teams solution to the challenge ‘Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer’, instead of embarking the players on space exploration, we challenge young players to face engineering challenges and face trade-offs to sustain a livable outpost on Mars. Through a simplified space engineering, it engages players even more and an enjoyable learning experience.

- User accessibility: the grid-based game is designed to be a simple interface for younger players to place modules

- Interactive feedback: log records beside the grid gives real-time signals to help maintain the outpost and experience the consequences of their decisions. 

- Scientific relevance: resource production, management, and consumption were designed while experiencing a real-world space challenge 

- Technical feasibility: the team focused on a functional gameplay mechanic using essential gameplay mechanics than complex features 

- Performance and accessibility: a simple browser game was chosen to make the game playable without advanced computer components or additional hardware and software installation 

Our team use real historical data from NASA spaceweather database, to replicate the solar flares. Additionally our team combines creative, educational, and accessible problem-solving game to younger audiences to the possibilities and challenges in space exploration on Mars.
